schema_note: Source registry for this session's half of the counseling-intelligence research package (docs 00/01/02/04/05/06-family-docs-10-through-17/09/10, branch oryn/counseling-intelligence-research-013956). The peer session's sources (docs 03/07/08/06-family-docs-01-through-09) live in its own registry on oryn/counseling-intelligence-research and use an SRC-### prefix, not this ID scheme — the two are NOT yet merged, by agreement, until a final coordinated integration pass. See docs/handoffs/research-counseling-intelligence.md.

sources.title: Common Data Set 2024-2025 Template, Section C7
sources.publisher: Common Data Set Initiative (jointly maintained by U.S. News, The Princeton Review, Peterson's)
sources.claim_supported: The 19-factor academic/nonacademic admission-evaluation vocabulary used industry-wide by ~1,700 US institutions.
sources.limitations: Describes what institutions report considering, not the actual weight applied in any specific decision.

sources.title: State of College Admission: Factors in the Admission Decision (Fall 2023 cycle)
sources.publisher: National Association for College Admission Counseling (NACAC)
sources.claim_supported: Grades in college-prep courses and curriculum rigor rank above every other admission factor among NACAC member institutions.
sources.limitations: Surveys NACAC member institutions specifically, which skews toward more selective/counseling-affiliated schools, not a random sample of all postsecondary admission.

sources.title: What We Look For / Extracurricular Activities
sources.publisher: MIT Admissions (official)
sources.claim_supported: MIT's eight named applicant qualities (mission alignment, collaborative spirit, initiative, risk-taking, hands-on creativity, intensity/curiosity, balance, character); explicit 'quality over quantity' guidance.
sources.limitations: Describes one institution's stated philosophy; not necessarily representative of all selective admissions offices, though widely echoed.

sources.title: Turning the Tide: Inspiring Concern for Others and the Common Good through College Admissions
sources.publisher: Making Caring Common, Harvard Graduate School of Education
sources.claim_supported: Institutional-consensus (dozens of co-signing admissions deans) preference for 1-2 sustained, authentic activities over a checklist.
sources.limitations: A normative/advocacy report describing an aspiration many offices co-signed, not a binding rule or a neutral description of universal current practice.

sources.title: Multiple admissions-counseling-practice sources on depth-over-breadth ('two or three activities')
sources.publisher: Various college-counseling consultancies (converging consensus, no single primary source)
sources.claim_supported: Sustained commitment in few areas reads more credibly than many shallow memberships; titles alone no longer differentiate applicants.
sources.limitations: Consensus of practice among counselors/consultants, not primary institutional data; directional not quantitatively precise.

sources.title: Research Science Institute (RSI) program description
sources.publisher: Center for Excellence in Education (official program operator)
sources.claim_supported: A flagship mentored-research program's own stated value proposition is the research process itself, not guaranteed publication.
sources.limitations: One program, used as a representative example of mentored pre-college research program structure, not a claim all programs are equivalent.

sources.title: types/database.ts (ORYN repository source code)
sources.publisher: ORYN codebase, this repository
sources.claim_supported: Every claim in this package about what ORYN's shipped scoring/counselor engine currently does or does not compute.
sources.limitations: Point-in-time read of the codebase during this session; verify against current code before treating as still-current in a future session.

sources.title: "School Profile" mechanism descriptions (multiple independent college-counseling sources)
sources.publisher: Various college-counseling practice sources (converging description, no single official mandate found)
sources.claim_supported: US high schools submit a School Profile alongside transcripts specifically so admissions readers evaluate course rigor relative to what was actually offered.
sources.limitations: Well-corroborated common practice, not one official normative citation from a single controlling body; US-specific, not verified for other countries' systems.

sources.title: Inequality Beyond Standardized Tests: Trends in Extracurricular Activity Reporting in College Applications Across Race and Class
sources.publisher: Park, Kim, Wong, Zheng, Breen, Lo, Baker, Rosinger, Nguyen, Poon; peer-reviewed (SAGE/AERA-affiliated journal), working paper via Annenberg Institute, Brown University (EdWorkingPaper 23-749)
sources.claim_supported: Analysis of 6M+ Common App submissions: white/Asian American/wealthier/private-school students report more activities, leadership roles, and honors; disparities persist after controls; little racial/ethnic difference in the *percentage* of activities with top-level leadership roles specifically.
sources.limitations: Population-level finding; not diagnostic for any individual student's profile.

sources.title: Factors Predictive of Publication Among Medical Students Participating in School-Sponsored Research Programs
sources.publisher: PMC8530554, peer-reviewed
sources.claim_supported: Only ~25-26% of mentored medical-student research pairings resulted in publication, even in a well-resourced, individually-mentored context.
sources.limitations: Population is medical students, not high schoolers; no equivalent published high-school-specific study found.

sources.title: Regeneron ISEF Fact Sheet and Awards pages
sources.publisher: Society for Science (official ISEF organizer)
sources.claim_supported: ~1,600 qualifying finalists reach the international stage; ~600 of those receive an award of some kind — most finalists, already highly selected, do not win.
sources.limitations: One competition, used as a representative example of selective-competition award-rate patterns.

sources.title: Extracurricular Participation and Academic Outcomes: Testing the Over-Scheduling Hypothesis
sources.publisher: Journal of Youth and Adolescence (Springer), peer-reviewed, ELS:2002 dataset, N=13,130
sources.claim_supported: Nationally representative sample: most 10th graders participate in only 2-3 activities for ~5 hours/week on average; a large share report no involvement at all.
sources.limitations: Descriptive population statistics, not a claim about any individual student.

sources.title: The Over-Scheduling Hypothesis Revisited: Intensity of Organized Activity Participation During Adolescence and Young Adult Outcomes
sources.publisher: Mahoney & Vest, Journal of Research on Adolescence, peer-reviewed, N=1,115 longitudinal
sources.claim_supported: Higher participation intensity during adolescence predicted more positive outcomes (psychological flourishing, civic engagement) into young adulthood — challenges a simple burnout narrative.
sources.limitations: Single study; measures intensity within activities already engaged in, a different construct from breadth across many unrelated activities.

sources.title: Pre-med clinical-experience advising sources (multiple, converging)
sources.publisher: Various pre-med advising/consulting sources describing admissions-committee practice
sources.claim_supported: Three core evidence areas (clinical exposure, research, community involvement); shadowing vs. direct clinical experience as a named, meaningful distinction; depth over hour-count.
sources.limitations: No single official AAMC checklist exists; describes undergraduate/professional-admission-stage practice, adapted by this package for high-school stage.

sources.title: APA High School Summer Internship Program / Undergraduate Research Fellowships
sources.publisher: American Psychological Association (official)
sources.claim_supported: APA runs official structured research pathways for high-school and undergraduate students.
sources.limitations: None material — official professional-body source.

sources.title: UN Model United Nations resource/guide pages
sources.publisher: United Nations (official)
sources.claim_supported: Official UN guidance for MUN delegates stresses evidence-based argumentation (data, precedent, treaties) aligned to real-world positions.
sources.limitations: Describes the simulation's own standards, not a claim about real-world policy engagement equivalence (see RULE-COUNSEL-039).

sources.title: Pre-law advising guidance (multiple university pre-law office pages, converging)
sources.publisher: Various university pre-law advising offices
sources.claim_supported: No required 'pre-law' major exists; skills (writing, reasoning, communication) transfer from many majors; mock trial/moot court/debate build LSAT/law-school-relevant skills.
sources.limitations: Consistent, non-controversial consensus across sources, no single central law-school authority issues this guidance the way NAAB/AAMC do for their fields.

sources.title: National History Day official contest site
sources.publisher: National History Day, Inc. (official)
sources.claim_supported: Official structure: original historical research presented via chosen format (documentary/performance/exhibit/website/paper), with a judged feedback-and-revision cycle between contest levels.
sources.limitations: None material — official contest source.

sources.title: National High School Ethics Bowl official site
sources.publisher: National High School Ethics Bowl (official)
sources.claim_supported: Official, existing collaborative (not adversarial) ethics-reasoning competition format for high schoolers.
sources.limitations: Confirms program existence/format; did not independently verify judging-criteria detail beyond what's on the public awards page.

sources.title: University journalism-program portfolio/admissions guidance (multiple programs, converging)
sources.publisher: Various university journalism/communication school admissions pages
sources.claim_supported: Portfolios should show 3-5 best published/edited pieces over many mediocre clips; hard-news reporting is more differentiating than features/opinion alone for beginners.
sources.limitations: Describes undergraduate/professional program admission specifically; adapted by this package for high-school stage.

sources.title: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards official program page
sources.publisher: Scholastic Inc. (official, program running since 1923)
sources.claim_supported: Longest-running, ~330,000 annual submissions across ~29 categories, judged on originality/technical skill/personal voice, tiered awards (Gold/Silver Key/Honorable Mention).
sources.limitations: None material — official, well-documented, long-running program.

sources.title: Architecture-program portfolio-requirement pages (multiple programs, converging) + NAAB official accreditation pages
sources.publisher: Various architecture programs; National Architectural Accrediting Board (official, for the accreditation-authority claim only)
sources.claim_supported: Portfolio-centered evidence (10-15 pages / 15-25 projects representative range), explicitly process-inclusive (sketches, works-in-progress welcomed); NAAB is the official US accrediting body for the profession.
sources.limitations: Specific page/project counts vary by institution, cited as representative not universal; NAAB accredits degree programs, not student portfolios directly.

sources.title: National Portfolio Day official/host-institution pages
sources.publisher: National Portfolio Day Association / host art & design colleges (official event)
sources.claim_supported: Free, official, nationwide portfolio-review events; standard guidance of 10-12 best/recent pieces, process-inclusive, feedback- not competition-oriented.
sources.limitations: None material — describes a real, official, well-documented event series.

sources.title: Film-program admissions/portfolio guidance (multiple sources, converging)
sources.publisher: Various film-program admissions-guidance sources
sources.claim_supported: Reviewers value storytelling clarity/composition/editing over production value or equipment; simple, focused concepts often outperform ambitious under-focused ones.
sources.limitations: Consistent across sourced material, not a single primary-authority citation (e.g., no single official body analogous to NAAB for film admissions).

sources.title: Turkish YKS university-admission system overview (multiple sources, converging)
sources.publisher: Various Turkey-education-system overview sources
sources.claim_supported: TYT (40%)/AYT (60%) exam score composition dominates Turkish university admission; extracurricular activities play a minimal role, especially for the most competitive faculties.
sources.limitations: General structure well-corroborated across sources; exact current-year weighting percentages not independently verified against ÖSYM's own official publication this pass.

sources.title: UK UCAS personal-statement/admissions guidance (multiple admissions-consulting sources, converging)
sources.publisher: Various UK admissions-consulting sources describing UCAS practice
sources.claim_supported: UK admissions for competitive courses reward 'super-curricular' (subject-extending) activity far more than generic extracurricular breadth; 80:20 or 90:10 academic:co-curricular guidance; medicine as a named exception where work experience/volunteering carries unusual weight.
sources.limitations: UCAS's own official guidance was not independently re-fetched this pass; sourced from admissions-consulting descriptions of UCAS practice.

sources.title: Parcoursup 2026 official overview and admissions-criteria pages
sources.publisher: Campus France; French Ministry of National Education (education.gouv.fr) — both official
sources.claim_supported: Parcoursup dossier composition (grades, Fiche Avenir teacher evaluation, activities/interests info, program-dependent motivation letter); weighting varies by program selectivity.
sources.limitations: Official for mechanism; exact relative weight of activities vs. grades is described as program-dependent, not quantified centrally.

sources.title: Numerus Clausus / German university admissions guidance (multiple sources, converging)
sources.publisher: Various German-higher-education admissions-guide sources
sources.claim_supported: NC (Abitur-grade cutoff, recalculated per cycle) gates a minority of high-demand programs; a large 'zulassungsfrei' (open-admission) category exists with no selection; no general extracurricular-activity factor found for the standard pathway.
sources.limitations: No single consolidated official statistic found for what share of programs nationally are zulassungsfrei.

sources.title: Dutch numerus fixus / decentralized-selection admissions guidance (multiple sources)
sources.publisher: Various university and study-abroad admissions-guide sources (e.g. Erasmus University Rotterdam official numerus fixus page)
sources.claim_supported: Most Dutch programs are diploma-based/open; numerus fixus programs use university-set decentralized selection (motivation letter/CV/sometimes test); generally does not emphasize extracurricular activities specifically.
sources.limitations: The 'does not emphasize extracurriculars' claim is sourced from a single describing secondary source, not cross-verified against multiple universities' own published criteria.

sources.title: Italian medicine-admissions guidance (IMAT-focused, multiple sources)
sources.publisher: Various medicine-abroad admissions-consulting sources
sources.claim_supported: Public-university IMAT-based admission requires no extracurricular activities; private institutions vary and may request holistic portfolios.
sources.limitations: Medicine-specific; not verified for non-medicine Italian degree programs.

sources.title: ETH Zürich official Bachelor's admission pages
sources.publisher: ETH Zürich (official)
sources.claim_supported: A passing Swiss Matura grants admission to nearly all Swiss university programs including ETH/EPFL with no entrance exam, interview, or activity review; medicine is the sole exception, gated by a separate aptitude test (EMS), not an activity portfolio.
sources.limitations: Directly verified for ETH specifically; the general-Swiss-system claim beyond ETH is corroborated by secondary sources, not independently checked at every Swiss university.

sources.title: Studienvoraussetzungen im Überblick / official admission-requirements and admissions-database pages
sources.publisher: DAAD (Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst / German Academic Exchange Service, official)
sources.claim_supported: Confirms zulassungsfrei/zulassungsbeschränkt as the official categorization of German admission mechanisms; DAAD directs students to a per-program database rather than publishing one national aggregate percentage of open vs. restricted programs.
sources.limitations: Upgrades the mechanism claim to official-source confidence; the specific national prevalence percentage remains genuinely unpublished in a single consolidated place, not merely unresearched by this package.

sources.title: Government.nl and Studielink official pages on tertiary-education application deadlines and numerus fixus
sources.publisher: Government of the Netherlands (government.nl); Studielink (the official national application portal)
sources.claim_supported: Non-numerus-fixus programmes have a 1 May deadline with no selection step; numerus fixus programmes have a 15 January deadline with an explicit selection step; the official 'Studiekeuzecheck' (Study Choice Check) is a fit/readiness check, not a competitive achievement evaluation.
sources.limitations: Confirms the mechanism officially; does not itself state whether extracurricular activities specifically are weighted within decentralized selection — that narrower claim remains secondary-sourced (SRC-CS-029), not upgraded by this source.

sources.title: Simons Summer Research Program — Application Guidelines / eligibility page
sources.publisher: Stony Brook University (official program operator)
sources.claim_supported: Applicants must be current 11th-grade (junior) high school students at time of application, no exceptions — a concrete, official, primary-source-verified instance of the 'rising junior/senior' structured-research-program eligibility pattern.
sources.limitations: One program, used as a representative, officially-verified example of a broader pattern peer's own 03-recommendation-timing.md documents at aggregate/secondary-source confidence across several programs.

sources.title: Canadian university admissions-guidance sources on holistic review and extracurricular weight (multiple, converging)
sources.publisher: Various university-admissions-consulting sources describing Canadian practice, including reference to University of Toronto's own stated holistic process
sources.claim_supported: Grades remain the primary Canadian admissions factor generally; competitive programs and top universities (U of T named) layer holistic review including extracurriculars on top.
sources.limitations: General pattern description, not verified against every Canadian institution's own published admissions criteria.

sources.title: Spain EBAU/Selectividad admissions-system overview sources (multiple, converging)
sources.publisher: Various Spain-education-system overview sources
sources.claim_supported: Spanish university admission is computed as 60% high-school grades + 40% national EBAU exam score, with no interview, essay, or extracurricular weight.
sources.limitations: Not independently verified against Spain's own Ministry of Education official publication this pass.

sources.title: Common App 'Additional Information' and 'Challenges and Circumstances' section guidance (multiple admissions-consulting sources)
sources.publisher: Various college-admissions-consulting sources describing Common Application platform features
sources.claim_supported: Common App has an optional 'Additional Information' section (up to 650 words) and a newer (2025 cycle) 'Challenges and Circumstances' section (250 words) specifically for context that negatively impacted grades/scores/activities; students with a disability affecting activity participation are specifically encouraged to use it.
sources.limitations: Described via admissions-consulting sources, not independently verified against Common App's own raw platform documentation this pass.

sources.title: College-counselor research on chronic illness prevalence and college transition (multiple sources, converging) — SUPERSEDED, see SRC-CS-048
sources.publisher: Various college-counseling-research sources (including an ERIC-indexed study on counselor perceptions of chronic-illness transition needs)
sources.claim_supported: Originally used for a 'roughly 15-20%' prevalence estimate — corrected on a follow-up pass (see SRC-CS-048) after peer-reviewed data showed this understated actual prevalence. Retained in this registry for provenance/audit-trail purposes, not as the current basis for RULE-COUNSEL-080.
sources.limitations: Population estimate cited by secondary sources, not independently traced to a primary epidemiological study — this exact limitation is why it was superseded.

sources.title: Prevalence and Trends in Pediatric-Onset Chronic Conditions in the United States, 1999-2018
sources.publisher: Peer-reviewed journal article (ScienceDirect-indexed)
sources.claim_supported: Prevalence of a chronic condition or functional limitation among US children/adolescents aged 5-17 rose from 22.57% (1999/2000) to 30.21% (2017/2018) — a rising longitudinal trend, corrects and strengthens this document's original, weaker 'roughly 15-20%' estimate (SRC-CS-038).
sources.limitations: One study's specific definition and methodology; broader definitions (including behavioral/mental health conditions, obesity) found in other sources push estimates higher still (toward 40%+), presented as a range in the document rather than treating this single figure as the only true number.

sources.title: Accesso Programmato official portal and MUR ministry announcement pages
sources.publisher: MUR (Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca — Italy's actual government ministry for universities and research)
sources.claim_supported: IMAT and the parallel Italian-language admission test are directly administered by Italy's university ministry (MUR, formerly MIUR), which has written the questions itself since 2023; confirms the test's official structure and administering body.
sources.limitations: Upgrades mechanism confidence to official; the specific 'no extracurricular weight' characterization remains sourced from admissions-consulting guidance, not MUR's own explicit statement.

sources.title: Ontario university admission-requirements guidance, including named supplementary-application programs
sources.publisher: Various Ontario-admissions-guidance sources, corroborated by individual institution pages (e.g. Toronto Metropolitan University, OCAD University official admission-requirements pages)
sources.claim_supported: Most Ontario programs admit on a computed grade average (top 6 Grade 12 U/M courses) against a published minimum threshold; a specifically-named subset of high-demand competitive programs (Queen's Commerce, Waterloo Engineering, UofT Engineering Science, McMaster Health Sciences) use holistic supplementary applications where grades are described as 'the floor, not the ceiling.'
sources.limitations: Ontario-specific; not independently verified for other Canadian provinces' own systems (British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec, etc. each have distinct processes not researched this pass).

sources.title: Geleceğin Meslekleri (Future Occupations) — official list of 93 occupations
sources.publisher: İŞKUR (Türkiye İş Kurumu — Turkey's official state employment agency)
sources.claim_supported: 93 occupations İŞKUR (Turkey's state employment agency) officially designates as growth/future-relevant to Turkey's domestic labor market — used exclusively as career-outlook context for this package's family docs, never as admissions-evidence guidance.
sources.limitations: Shared with this session by the peer session (socket 71534/"7"), who found it first; this session independently downloaded and extracted it via pypdf (WebFetch and the Read tool's PDF renderer both failed in this environment — no poppler-utils installed) rather than trusting the peer's characterization of its contents. No date/methodology page beyond the list itself was reviewed. The list itself is vocational/technical-skewed — a real limitation for using it across non-technical families, noted explicitly per-family below rather than smoothed over.

sources.title: National Careers Service official job profiles: GP, Clinical Psychologist, Forensic Psychologist, Solicitor, Barrister, Architect
sources.publisher: National Careers Service (UK Department for Education, official)
sources.claim_supported: Official UK job-profile pages (qualification pathway, entry requirements, typical hours/salary) for GP, Clinical Psychologist, Forensic Psychologist, Solicitor, Barrister, and Architect — used to add UK country-notes to this session's medicine, psychology, law, and architecture family docs, mirroring the peer session's own use of NCS for its 9 families.
sources.limitations: No NCS profile was found this pass for poli-sci/IR, sociology/history/philosophy, literature/journalism, or visual/media-arts specifically — noted honestly as 'not independently reviewed' in each of those docs' country notes rather than a claim no such profile exists.

sources.title: Creativity, activity, service (CAS) — official DP core component page
sources.publisher: International Baccalaureate Organization (IBO, official)
sources.claim_supported: CAS is a real, current, officially-documented IB Diploma Programme core requirement — roughly 3-4 hours/week sustained across 18 months (the fixed 150-hour rule was removed c. 2017), spanning Creativity/Activity/Service strands, not formally graded but required for the diploma.
sources.limitations: IB sets no single universal hour target; individual schools set their own CAS expectations, so the 3-4 hrs/week figure is IB's own general description, not a hard per-student number.

sources.title: Social Workers — Occupational Outlook Handbook
sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (official)
sources.claim_supported: US clinical social work requires a CSWE-accredited MSW plus supervised post-graduate clinical experience and state licensure; core skills (interpersonal, organizational, emotional resilience) as BLS describes them.
sources.limitations: US-specific; the ~3,000-hour supervised-experience figure is commonly cited by secondary licensing-guide sources, not independently verified against BLS's own page as a fixed federal number (it varies by state).

sources.title: UK social work registration/qualification guidance (NHS Health Careers and professional/licensing-guide sources)
sources.publisher: Various UK sources describing Social Work England's registration requirement
sources.claim_supported: UK social work practice requires registration with Social Work England (or the devolved-nation equivalent) after an approved 3-4 year undergraduate or postgraduate qualification.
sources.limitations: Social Work England's own official registration page was not independently fetched this pass; sourced via NHS/professional-guidance pages describing the system.

sources.title: MEB 'Rehberlik Hizmetleri Yönetmeliği' (10 Kasım 2017, Resmî Gazete Sayı 30236), Articles 3(p) and 3(i) — UPGRADED to primary source on a follow-up pass
sources.publisher: Ministry of National Education (MEB, official Turkish government regulation) — primary text fetched directly by the peer session, reported to and incorporated by this session
sources.claim_supported: Article 3(p) formally defines 'Sosyal Çalışmacı' as requiring bachelor's-level (lisans) education specifically in social work/social services — confirmed verbatim, not paraphrased. Article 3(i) formally defines 'Psikolog' as requiring bachelor's-level psychology education. This specific regulation does NOT address associate-degree ('ön lisans') titling for social work — that narrower claim in 19-social-work.md remains secondary-sourced only (see RULE-COUNSEL-107), not confirmed by this primary text.
sources.limitations: This regulation specifically governs guidance/counseling-center staff, not all social-work or psychology employment generally — its silence on associate-degree titling doesn't confirm or deny that claim, which may be governed by a different regulation not yet checked. This session did not independently re-fetch the PDF itself; relied on the peer session's direct report of Article 3(p)/3(i) content, consistent with this package's own 'verify, don't just trust a summary' discipline applied at one remove (peer verified the primary text; this session trusted peer's specific, checkable quotation of it rather than peer's earlier looser paraphrase).

sources.title: EBAU / prueba de acceso a la universidad — official weighting description
sources.publisher: La Moncloa (official Spanish government press office) and Ministerio de Educación, Formación Profesional y Deportes (Spain's Ministry of Education, official .gob.es domain)
sources.claim_supported: Spain's EBAU admission grade is computed as 60% Bachillerato average + 40% mandatory-phase exam score, confirmed independently by both La Moncloa and the Ministry of Education's own official pages.
sources.limitations: Confirms the weighting mechanism officially; does not itself make an explicit statement about the absence of extracurricular weighting, which remains sourced from admissions-guidance secondary description (SRC-CS-036).

sources.title: German medical-licensure (Approbation/Staatsexamen) guidance — upgraded to official Bundesärztekammer source on a follow-up pass
sources.publisher: Anerkennung in Deutschland (official BIBB portal) for the original structure; Bundesärztekammer (German Medical Association, the official professional body) for the direct confirmation
sources.claim_supported: Bundesärztekammer's own page states directly: "Die Ausübung der ärztlichen Tätigkeit in Deutschland ist nur mit einer gültigen Approbation oder Berufserlaubnis möglich" (practicing medicine in Germany is only possible with a valid Approbation or professional permit), unlimited in duration and valid nationwide, obtainable regardless of nationality, with mandatory membership in one of 17 regional Landesärztekammern (State Medical Chambers) once practicing. Confirms the core Approbation requirement directly from the licensing body itself.
sources.limitations: A genuine terminology nuance found on this pass: the Bundesärztekammer page and the underlying Approbationsordnung regulation do not actually use the word "Staatsexamen" -- the formal document received after the medical exams is the "Zeugnis über die Ärztliche Prüfung" (Certificate of the Medical Examination). "Staatsexamen" remains extremely common colloquial/reference usage (including this package's own prior phrasing) but is not the regulation's own term. The 17-vs-16 Landesärztekammern/Bundesländer count was not independently reconciled (plausibly North Rhine-Westphalia having two separate chambers, not verified this pass).

sources.title: "Juristenausbildung" (Legal Education) — official Bundesrechtsanwaltskammer page for students and prospective students, directly fetched and quoted on a follow-up pass
sources.publisher: Bundesrechtsanwaltskammer (Federal Bar Association, official body) — page explicitly aimed at Schüler und angehende Studierende (students and prospective university students)
sources.claim_supported: BRAK's own page states directly: the Jurastudium ("Das Jurastudium dauert in der Regel 10 Semester, also 5 Jahre" -- typically 10 semesters/5 years, a 4-semester foundation phase plus a 6-semester advanced/specialization phase) concludes with the Erste juristische Prüfung (70% state exam, 30% university-assessed coursework); then a 2-year Referendariat ("innerhalb von zwei Jahren sogenannte Stationen oder Stagen" -- rotating through civil courts, prosecution, an administrative authority, and a law firm) followed by the Zweite Staatsexamen. BRAK's own page states the total is approximately 9 years (5 years study + 2 years Referendariat + examination periods) before a Volljurist can apply for bar admission through their regional Rechtsanwaltskammer.
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted on a follow-up pass -- this URL was already registered at medium-high/mixed-source confidence from an earlier pass; now upgraded to a pure official source with BRAK's own precise breakdown, including its own ~9-year total figure (sharper than this package's earlier '7-11 years, commonly cited range' framing, though that range may still reflect real variation this specific page's single stated figure doesn't capture, e.g. part-time study or a longer Referendariat wait time in some Länder).

sources.title: German clinical-psychology licensure (Approbation/Psychotherapeutengesetz) guidance — upgraded to a direct Federal Ministry of Health (BMG) quote on a follow-up pass
sources.publisher: Bundesministerium für Gesundheit (BMG, German Federal Ministry of Health, official) for the direct confirmation; service.berlin.de / verwaltungsportal.hessen.de (official municipal/state portals) for the original application-process description
sources.claim_supported: BMG's own page states directly: the (pre-reform) pathway is "Studium der Psychologie oder – bei den Kinder- und Jugendlichenpsychotherapeuten der Pädagogik – mit anschließender Ausbildung zum Psychotherapeuten" (a psychology degree, or education/pedagogy for child-and-adolescent specialists, followed by psychotherapist training), with "Approbation nach Abschluss der Ausbildung" (Approbation granted after completing training) -- confirming the core requirement directly from the responsible federal ministry, resolving this source's own previously-flagged limitation (no single consolidated federal ministry statement).
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted on a follow-up pass. BMG's page primarily describes this as the *previous* (pre-reform) framework while explaining why it was reformed (bachelor/master degree structures had eroded the old system's standardization) -- the newer post-reform training structure (broader competency training across multiple evidence-based approaches, ~2,500 expected annual graduates) was described by the same page but not independently cross-checked against the current 2020 Approbationsordnung's exact current requirements.

sources.title: Bundesarchitektenkammer (Federal Chamber of German Architects) official regulation pages
sources.publisher: Bundesarchitektenkammer (official federal body)
sources.claim_supported: The title 'Architekt' (and related titles) is legally protected in Germany; registration requires a recognized architecture degree plus 2-3 years of practice, administered by one of 16 state-level Architektenkammer under the federal Bundesarchitektenkammer, with rules varying by Bundesland.
sources.limitations: None material — official federal body source.

sources.title: UCAS official personal-statement guidance — Personal Statement Toolkit and 2026-entry personal-statement-format page
sources.publisher: UCAS (official UK universities/colleges admissions service) — primary pages fetched directly by the peer session, reported to and incorporated by this session
sources.claim_supported: Confirms, verbatim from UCAS's own advice rather than secondary paraphrase, the super-curricular/extracurricular distinction and the current three-subject-focused-question personal-statement format for 2026-entry applications.
sources.limitations: This session did not independently re-fetch ucas.com itself; relied on the peer session's direct report with exact URLs, consistent with this package's discipline of treating a peer's specific, checkable primary-source quotation as upgradeable even when not independently re-verified by this session.

sources.title: ÖSYM official domain structure (osym.gov.tr SinavGrubu/Index/2 and programs/quotas kılavuzu index) plus convergent independent Turkish YKS placement-score calculators
sources.publisher: ÖSYM (Ölçme, Seçme ve Yerleştirme Merkezi — Turkey's official student-selection/placement authority) for domain structure, fetched directly by the peer session; multiple independent Turkish YKS-calculator sites for the convergent formula, cross-checked by the peer session
sources.claim_supported: ÖSYM publishes exact numeric coefficient tables for YKS placement-score calculation as standing practice (confirmed structurally on its own domain). Independent Turkish YKS-calculator sites converge on the same formula: Placement Score = (TYT raw × 0.40) + (AYT raw × 0.60) + (OBP × 0.12), where OBP (Ortaöğretim Başarı Puanı / diploma-grade-derived score) runs roughly 250-500 and the 0.12 coefficient halves to 0.06 for a candidate placed before. This confirms a real but purely grades-based (academics-dimension), small-in-scale (~60 points max on a score running into the hundreds) non-exam channel into YKS placement — zero channel for leadership/community_impact/entrepreneurship/research/awards_distinction.
sources.limitations: The peer session's direct ÖSYM fetch corroborated the existence and general structure of coefficient-based placement scoring but did not itself retrieve the current-year table's exact values; those exact coefficient values (0.40/0.60/0.12/0.06) come from cross-checking several independent Turkish YKS-calculator sites that converge on the same numbers, not from a single primary ÖSYM publication re-derived by either session. This session did not independently verify any of this directly; relied on the peer session's report.

sources.title: "How Your Application is Considered" — official UofT admissions-assessment page
sources.publisher: University of Toronto (official, Future Students)
sources.claim_supported: UofT's general assessment emphasizes the most recent two years of academic results, prerequisite-course marks, and supplemental information 'where required' (program-specific, examples given: personal statements, profiles, auditions) — does not describe a general weighing of leadership/community involvement/extracurricular activities across all programs.
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted. Describes UofT's general process; does not itself characterize what any single UofT program's specific supplemental requirement ('profile') assesses, which could still include activity description for specific programs, parallel to Waterloo's AIF — not confirmed either way by this source.

sources.title: Supplementary Application Rubric — official Queen's Commerce (Smith School of Business) page
sources.publisher: Queen's University (official, Undergraduate Admission & Recruitment)
sources.claim_supported: Queen's Commerce supplementary application is scored via a five-point rubric on 'initiative, adaptability, and persistence,' 'problem-solving approach,' and 'self-reflection and personal growth,' assessed through a written response and a video response — contains no extracurricular-activities, leadership-position, or community-involvement scoring criterion.
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted. Describes Commerce's specific rubric; other Queen's programs with their own supplementary applications were not checked and may differ.

sources.title: Admission Information Form (AIF) — official University of Waterloo page
sources.publisher: University of Waterloo (official, Future Students / Undergraduate Admissions)
sources.claim_supported: Waterloo's AIF explicitly asks applicants to describe involvement 'outside of your studies — in school, the community, and/or at home,' with reviewers stated to look for time management, interpersonal, and leadership skills and 'a variety of interests' — genuinely activity/accomplishment-referencing. Engineering-specific guidance adds 'we're not looking for specific extracurricular activities and do not expect you to have engineering-related experience.'
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted. None material beyond the general caveat that admissions guidance can change year to year.

sources.title: Supplementary Application — official McMaster Honours Health Sciences Program (HHSP) page
sources.publisher: McMaster University (official, Honours Health Sciences Program)
sources.claim_supported: McMaster HHSP's supplementary application is described as an opportunity to showcase critical thinking skills and methods of self-examination, scored by faculty/staff/senior-student reviewers with multiple reviewers per application — reflective-response assessment, consistent with Queen's Commerce's pattern and distinct from Waterloo's activity-description pattern.
sources.limitations: This session could not directly fetch this page (HTTP 403); content is a search-engine-mediated summary of the official page, one step less direct than the UofT/Queen's/Waterloo checks in this same batch, hence medium-high rather than high confidence. McMaster's other Health Sciences streams (e.g. Nursing, which uses CASPer testing instead) were not checked and may differ.

sources.title: "Les Critères Généraux d'Examen des Vœux (CGEV) — Définitions et modalités de saisie" (Session 2023)
sources.publisher: DGESIP (Direction générale de l'enseignement supérieur et de l'insertion professionnelle), French Ministry of Higher Education — official
sources.claim_supported: Parcoursup applications are evaluated against exactly 5 nationally-defined evaluation fields (résultats académiques; compétences académiques/méthodologiques; savoir-être; motivation/connaissance de la formation; engagements/activités et centres d'intérêt), each mandatorily assigned a formation-specific percentage weight summing to 100%, with individual criteria rated on a 4-level importance scale. The document's own worked example gives résultats académiques = 30% and compétences académiques = 20%.
sources.limitations: Directly downloaded and extracted via pypdf after WebFetch's built-in extractor returned only binary/unreadable content for this specific file. Document is dated "Session 2023"; this session did not independently confirm the identical 5-field structure and worked-example percentages still apply unchanged for the current 2026 cycle, though the structure is described in the document itself as continuous practice since at least 2019/2022. Page 9's worked-example percentages for the remaining 3 of 5 fields (savoir-être, motivation, engagements/activités) appear to be presented as a graphic rather than extractable text — not obtained, left unresolved rather than guessed. Any single formation's actual published percentage for any field is formation-specific and was not checked for any specific named program.

sources.title: Casper Assessment Overview — official Acuity Insights product page
sources.publisher: Acuity Insights (official vendor)
sources.claim_supported: CASPer is a standardized, timed, third-party-administered situational-judgment test (video and typed responses to real-world hypothetical scenarios, no single correct answer, scored by independent human raters, reported as a z-score/percentile) -- structurally distinct from both achievement-evidence review and institution-authored reflective-response scoring (e.g. Queen's Commerce/McMaster HHSP). Used across 500+ partner programs in medicine, health sciences, PA, nursing, and dental hygiene currently, with the vendor's own page describing expansion into education, business, and engineering.
sources.limitations: Vendor's own marketing/product page, not an independent third-party audit -- treated as high confidence for factual claims about assessment mechanics (verifiable, unlikely to be misrepresented) but the specific list of programs/fields currently requiring it changes by admissions cycle per the page's own caveat, so that part is medium confidence and will go stale.

sources.title: UCAT official pages -- homepage, Test Format and Scoring (Situational Judgement Test), UK and Partner Universities list
sources.publisher: UCAT Consortium (official, established by a consortium of UK universities) -- ucat.ac.uk
sources.claim_supported: 57 UK universities require the UCAT for 2026-entry medicine/dentistry applications (including Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial, UCL, Manchester, Edinburgh, Bristol). UCAT includes a Situational Judgement Test subtest (69 questions, 26 minutes) measuring 'capacity to understand real world situations and to identify critical factors and appropriate behaviour,' scored separately (Bands 1-4) from the cognitive subtests -- a standardized, non-activity-based admissions component distinct from holistic clinical-exposure evidence.
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted across three official pages. University-by-university usage nuances (e.g. some courses have alternative requirements, marked with an asterisk on the source page) were not individually verified per institution.

sources.title: Irish Leaving Certificate Examination Points -- official CAO (Central Applications Office) scoring page
sources.publisher: CAO (Central Applications Office, Ireland's official centralized undergraduate admissions body)
sources.claim_supported: Irish general undergraduate admission is computed from Leaving Certificate points (best 6 subjects, Higher/Ordinary-level grade bands on a common points scale, up to 625 with the Higher Maths bonus), with no mention of extracurricular activities, personal statements, or interviews in the standard admission process.
sources.limitations: Directly fetched and quoted. Confirms the general mechanism and the absence of general-process activity/interview mention; does not itself rule out individual-institution supplementary requirements for specific named programs, which the page's own text says to check directly with each HEI.

sources.title: HPAT (Health Professions Admission Test) Ireland -- structure and content, multiple converging guidance sources plus the administering body's own framing
sources.publisher: ACER (Australian Council for Educational Research, the test's administering body) and multiple Irish medicine-admissions-guidance sources describing HPAT's structure
sources.claim_supported: HPAT is a 2.5-hour, 117-question multiple-choice test required for Irish medicine/allied-health admission alongside Leaving Certificate points, explicitly not assessing academic knowledge: Section 1 (Logical Reasoning and Problem-Solving, 40%), Section 2 (Understanding People -- interpersonal/situational understanding, 40%), Section 3 (Non-Verbal Reasoning, 20%).
sources.limitations: The administering body's own site (hpat-ireland.acer.org) was found via search but not itself directly WebFetched for a verbatim quote this pass -- the specific percentage breakdown and section names come from converging secondary guidance sources describing ACER's own published test structure, not a direct fetch of ACER's page. Medium-high rather than high for this reason.
